feed.subtitle: I am a fourth-year Ph.D. student in Statistics and Data Science at Northwestern University, working on LLM forecasting. My recent research asks how to make LLM backtests reliable, with temporal leakage (look-ahead bias) as a central obstacle. I also study the robustness of LLM forecasting systems to manipulated evidence, and the interpretation of LLM predictions. Outside of research, I am deeply committed to an active lifestyle. I follow a structured workout program and train almost every day, viewing physical discipline as a natural complement to intellectual rigor. I enjoy a wide range of sports, with basketball being my favorite, and I am particularly drawn to long-distance running for both its physical demands and its meditative rhythm. These activities keep me grounded, energized, and continuously motivated—both on and off the track.
